cases.title: the rewrite applies inside string literals
cases.note: the recorded value is the rewritten literal

cases.title: a longer name ending in a helper's is rewritten
variable, resource and flow_user_state are each awaited
a call inside another is awaited inside it
a call that ends where the next begins closes first
a parenthesis inside a string counts
a call whose parentheses never close is awaited to the end
cases.note: an unclosed call ends at the end of its part, here the end of the text (JE-11, confirmed for request 8 of docs/design/README.md)

cases.title: JE-12 rewrites the result of JE-11
past a two-byte character the inserted ) lands a byte early, inside the string
cases.note: the position is counted in characters from the call and applied as a byte offset (JE-11, corrected 2026-10-28, request 8); the code leaves a parenthesis open, so the source does not compile; not yet recorded (Q-JE-13)

cases.title: where the ) would land inside a character, Windmill's evaluator panics
cases.note: the part after the call, "éé"), is 7 bytes and 5 characters; its ) is the fifth character, so the insertion goes at byte 4 of the part, byte 13 of the text, inside the second é (JE-11)

cases.title: a character before the call moves nothing
cases.note: the count starts at the call, just after its opening parenthesis, so text before it shifts nothing (JE-11, corrected 2026-10-29 for design request 10; FU3 had counted from the start of the text)

cases.title: a later helper's pass counts from its own call too
cases.note: each helper's pass cuts the text the previous one produced at its own call text (JE-11)

cases.title: a call nested in a call of the same helper cuts the outer one short
cases.note: the text is cut at every occurrence of the call text, and each part gets its own ), so the outer call's part ends where the inner call starts and never balances (JE-11); a call of another helper nests (variant nested)

cases.title: an unclosed call's ) goes before the next call of the same helper
the count starts at the call, so non-ASCII text before it shifts nothing
cases.note: a count from the start of the text would put the ) one byte early

cases.title: non-ASCII text inside the call moves the ) early by its extra bytes
cases.note: two characters are counted before the call's ), and the ) is inserted at byte 2 of the part, just after the two-byte é

cases.title: a call that never closes gets its ) at the end of its part
cases.note: the ) is inserted at the end of the text, where it closes the expression's own (

cases.title: an insertion inside a multi-byte character fails the evaluation with the runtime's panic report
cases.note: the ) would go at byte 1 of the part, inside the two-byte é, which is byte 11 of the text; <n> is the task number, which differs between runs; an input transform wraps the message in its own text (JE-23), which internal/engine checks

engine.error: task <n> panicked with message "assertion failed: self.is_char_boundary(idx)"

cases.title: text that is ASCII up to the insertion point is rewritten exactly
an unclosed call's ) at the end of the text is counted in characters too
cases.note: the character count places an unclosed call's ) too, at the end of its part (JE-11, confirmed 2026-10-29 for design request 10)
